title: DPDP Act 2023: Complete Statutory Compliance Guide for Indian Healthcare & Diagnostic Centers
meta_description: Comprehensive compliance roadmap for pathology laboratories, diagnostic chains, and clinics under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023.
summary: Everything pathology lab owners, radiologists, and hospital administrators need to know about Section 5 multilingual notices, Section 6 consent withdrawal, and Section 33 audit log retention.
content:
1. Overview of DPDP 2023 for Healthcare

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 imposes stringent statutory obligations on healthcare providers operating as Data Fiduciaries. Health records, diagnostic reports, and biometric identifiers are classified as sensitive personal data requiring verified lawful consent before processing.

2. Section 5 Notice Obligations

Prior to collecting patient phone numbers, Aadhaar, or diagnostic samples, clinics must serve a clear, itemized notice available in English and any 8th Schedule constitutional language applicable to their operational state.

3. Section 33 Immutable Access Logs

LIMS and EHR systems must maintain tamper-evident digital records documenting every access event by staff, laboratory technicians, and third-party referral doctors.

faqs.question: Are small independent clinics exempt from DPDP compliance?
faqs.answer: No. The DPDP Act 2023 applies to all entities processing digital personal data within India, regardless of annual turnover or patient volume.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Violations of personal data security safeguards under Section 33 can attract penalties up to ₹250 Crores per incident.

title: DPDP Compliance Guide for Diagnostic Centres in Maharashtra (2026)
meta_description: Complete statutory guide for pathology labs and diagnostic centres in Maharashtra to achieve DPDP Act 2023 Section 5 and Section 33 compliance.
summary: Pathology laboratories across Mumbai, Pune, and Nagpur must implement Section 5 bilingual consent notices (Marathi and English) before processing blood and radiology diagnostics.
content:
Section 5 Multilingual Notice Requirements in Maharashtra

Under Section 5(1) of the DPDP Act 2023, every data fiduciary operating diagnostic branches must provide notice in English and the 8th Schedule language of the state. In Maharashtra, pathology intake software must present consent options in Marathi alongside English prior to taking patient samples.

Section 33 Audit Obligations for LIMS Software

Maharashtra diagnostic chains storing electronic health records (EHR) must maintain tamper-evident audit trails recording every technician and doctor accessing patient lab reports.

faqs.question: Is Marathi consent notice mandatory for pathology labs in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The DPDP Act requires notices to be available in English and any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India applicable to the operational territory.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-compliance under Section 33 in Maharashtra?
faqs.answer: Failure to observe data security safeguards and audit integrity can attract statutory penalties up to ₹250 Crores under the DPDP Act 2023.

title: Sending Lab Reports via WhatsApp: Legal DPDP Rules for Clinics
meta_description: Learn how diagnostic centres can legally send PDF blood test reports via WhatsApp under Section 6 of DPDP Act 2023 without violating patient privacy.
summary: WhatsApp dispatch of diagnostic reports requires explicit opt-in consent and password-protected PDF payloads to satisfy statutory data privacy rules.
content:
The Risk of Unsolicited WhatsApp PDF Reports

Dispatching unencrypted medical reports to WhatsApp numbers without verified consent constitutes unconsented digital processing under Section 6 of the DPDP Act.

How to Secure WhatsApp Delivery Compliantly

1. Capture an opt-in checkbox during patient reception intake.
2. Encrypt the outgoing PDF report using patient date-of-birth or mobile last digits as password key.
3. Log the outbound dispatch hash into your Section 33 compliance register.

faqs.question: Can clinics send reports on WhatsApp automatically?
faqs.answer: Only if the patient explicitly checked the digital communication consent box during reception registration.

faqs.question: Does ConsentLayer integrate with WhatsApp Business API?
faqs.answer: Yes, ConsentLayer generates verifiable audit tokens that can be attached to WhatsApp automated webhook dispatches.
